title: Fix the Mistyped Constructor Name
description: The program should create a Book object with a title set through its constructor.
expectedBehavior: The program should print '1984', the book's title.
actualProblem: A real constructor cannot have a return type — writing 'public void Book(...)' makes this an ordinary method named Book, not a constructor. Java then only has the implicit no-argument default constructor, so new Book("1984") fails to compile because no constructor accepts a String.
explanation: A constructor is defined with the exact same name as the class and no return type at all — not even void. Adding a return type like void turns it into a regular method instead, so it's never called automatically when the object is created.
